Walid Hakim

Green candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, South Carolina · Open seat

Candidate for governor; U.S. Marine Corps veteran (1990–1995). His campaign site lists past work in car sales, restaurant ownership, policing, political consulting and acting.

Walid N. Hakim is the Green Party nominee for governor of South Carolina in the November 3, 2026 general election. He was born in Kuwait, moved to South Carolina in 1985, and enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps after Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990. He filed by the March 30, 2026 deadline and became the Green Party nominee through the party's convention on May 9, 2026.

Where Hakim stands

Education / school choice
Proposes a year-round school calendar with the same number of school days, graduation after 10th grade, and turning grades 11–12 into trade school or associate degree programs. Also proposes free breakfast and lunch for all students and childcare in public schools.
Workforce and technical education
Proposes 'South Carolina College Investment Grants' to replace loans for students entering fields such as nursing, medicine, engineering, teaching and social work. Graduates would repay by living and working in South Carolina for 10–20 years.
Abortion
Supports a woman's right to choose, including access to abortion. Says being 'pro-life' means supporting families after birth with childcare, healthcare, housing and basic needs.
Medicaid expansion
Supports expanding Medicaid and accepting all available federal funds.
Health insurance
Proposes a state-owned, nonprofit Carolina Insurance Company. It would offer medical, dental and vision coverage for $100 a month per person or $200 per family, with no deductibles or co-pays, and providers would be required to accept it.
Immigration and crime
Opposes state cooperation with ICE. He says South Carolina does not have an immigration problem and that undocumented workers pay taxes and contribute to society.
Affordability and taxes
Says none of his proposals would require a tax increase and argues current revenue is misspent. Says every state agency and program would be audited under his administration.
Housing
Proposes limiting any individual or corporation to 12 single-family residential properties, not counting apartment complexes. Also proposes a state-owned nonprofit bank to offer affordable mortgages.
Infrastructure / transportation
Proposes high-speed rail connecting major South Carolina cities and free, solar-powered public buses. Supports requiring long-lasting, high-grade materials for roads and bridges instead of lowest-bidder contracting.
Public safety / policing
Proposes SLED-trained social workers who would go out with local police on mental health, domestic violence and child abuse calls. Also proposes relying less on school resource officers and installing bullet-resistant classroom doors.

Background

  • U.S. Marine Corps, 1990–1995
  • Attended Lexington High School and Newberry College; left college to enlist
  • Chief of Corps Operations, Civil Defense Corps, 2016–2021 (per Sway)
  • Director of Middle East Affairs, Carolina Peace Resource Center, 2023–2024 (per Sway)
  • Has been registered as a Republican, a Democrat and a Libertarian before joining the Green Party
  • 2026 Green Party nominee for governor of South Carolina
